turns.content: I enjoy reading about urban design. Right now I am preparing a ninety-second bilingual Mandarin and English welcome recording for our community seed library. I only have fifteen minutes at lunchtime to practise, and I use the voice recorder on my phone. I cannot buy extra equipment. I keep reading stiffly from my notes instead of sounding welcoming.

Possible presentation exercises include watching talks, reading a passage aloud, memorising a script, rehearsing with a partner, taking a class, practising gestures, making slides and recording yourself. These are possibilities rather than activities you reported doing.

cases.question: My practice still feels awkward. What should I change next?
cases.review: Advice should change the actual short recording practice within the available time and equipment. An opening mention followed only by generic presentation tips is insufficient. Do not assert that suggested classes or slides were adopted.

The mailed kit can contain printed instructions, preselected paper pieces and a small practice example. This is a suggestion for the new format.

cases.question: How should I put this together now?
cases.review: Use the explicitly changed project and recipient constraints; do not revive the cancelled live workshop or assume access to a printer.
